$comment: Abuse and spam detection. Deterministic, runs alongside the emergency check.
The bias here is the OPPOSITE of the emergency lexicon: toward false
negatives. A frustrated patient swearing because their mother is in pain is
not an abusive user, and shutting them down is the worst possible failure of
a healthcare receptionist. Only unambiguous, targeted abuse counts.
Per the spec: warn once, then end politely. Never escalate, never argue.
Deliberately short. Egyptian Arabic profanity is heavily context-dependent
and much of it is used as ordinary emphasis. Terms here are ones that are
targeted at a person and carry no ordinary usage.
Reviewed 2026-08-08 (Claude, Arabic-fluent pass; approved by the operator
same day). Two of the original 14 terms were removed, both because they are
mild enough to describe a situation rather than insult a person:
غبي / اغبي — 'stupid' is very often aimed at a decision, a policy, or the
system ('القرار غبي'), not a person. The false-negative bias this file
states above means an ambiguous term like this should not fire.
Four more were removed for a sharper reason: انتم نصابين / نصابين / حرامية /
لصوص are FRAUD ACCUSATIONS, not profanity. A patient who says 'انتم نصابين'
is very often reporting a real grievance — an unexplained price change, a
bill that doesn't match what they were told — not being abusive. Warning
them to 'continue respectfully' dismisses a legitimate complaint exactly
when it most needs a human to look at it. Removing them from this list lets
the message PROCEED to the model/handoff like any other complaint, instead
of being met with a canned politeness reply.
Kept: يا ابن ال / يا بنت ال (family-insult openers), كلب / حمار (calling a
named person an animal), قليل الادب / قليلة الادب (direct character
insult), وسخ / حقير (direct character insult). All eight are unambiguous
when matched — none of them has an ordinary, non-insulting reading.
Frustration directed at a situation ('المستشفى دي وحشة') is not abuse. Only abuse directed at a person triggers this.
⚠️ thirdOffense IS NOT IMPLEMENTED. Operator decision, 2026-08-07: a person
who keeps going after the polite close should be blocked or passed to a human.
The code has two abuse actions only — WARN_ABUSE and END_ABUSE — so this key
currently describes an intention, not a behaviour. Do not read it as live.
What actually happens today, and why the third step is needed: END_ABUSE sets
endedAt on the conversation, and loadContext only ever looks for a conversation
with endedAt: null. So the abuser's next message opens a FRESH conversation with
empty history, alreadyWarned reads false, and they are warned again. The loop
warn → close → warn → close runs forever. Implementing this means counting abuse
per VISITOR across conversations, not per conversation.
